case_study_insert.main_stem: Transgreen Logistics (TGL) is a cooperative in the recycling and green freight sector, employing a workforce of 70. Founded in 2012 by Nia Okafor, it collects and processes recyclable materials for local authorities and runs a flat structure with democratic leadership. TGL plans to invest $540,000 in an electric collection-truck fleet and a computerised stock control system, financed by a $340,000 bank loan and $200,000 retained profit. It has fixed costs of $200,000 a year, a variable cost of $4.00 a unit and a selling price of $9.00, and currently handles 100,000 units a year. TGL faces an operational problem: load contamination has reached 5.6% and vehicle defect rates are rising, while its depot reports growing fuel waste from older diesel vehicles.
case_study_insert.appendix_1_marketing_ops: Operations and Quality Report — Q3 2025: The fleet completed 26,000 collections last quarter with a contamination rate of 5.6%, down from 7.2% a year ago. Customer complaints fell from 41 to 23 per month. Average collection time is 3.7 days and the vehicle defect rate is 4.1%. Fuel waste is 8% of mileage. Market research of 450 local authority officers found 63% would pay $0.30 more for guaranteed contamination-free collections, and 59% rank reliability above price. A review shows 19 of 70 drivers have not completed on-the-job training on the electric trucks; off-the-job training at the regional college is also being considered. Managers are considering job rotation and team working to cut contamination and vehicle defects.

appendix_2_financial_data.title: Extract from the Statement of Profit or Loss and Capital employed data of Transgreen Logistics for the year ended 31 March 2025 ($ '000)

case_study_insert.appendix_3_external_environment: Economic and Business Bulletin (November 2026): (1) The central bank has raised the base interest rate from 4.25% to 5.0%, increasing borrowing costs for firms with variable-rate loans. (2) The national minimum wage will rise by 5.9% from $12.50 to $13.35 an hour from April 2026, raising wage bills across the recycling sector. (3) Diesel and recycling input costs have risen 10.1% year-on-year, waste-services inflation is 7.6%, and demand for recycled materials grew 3.9%.

questions.question_text: TGL plans to fund part of its $540,000 electric-fleet investment with $200,000 retained profit. Explain two advantages for TGL of using retained profit instead of the $340,000 bank loan.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Retained profit costs no interest or repayments, protecting the cash flow of a cooperative with fixed costs of $200,000 a year and a $340,000 bank loan. The saving can be used to cut the 5.6% contamination rate and the 8% fuel waste without raising the $9.00 selling price to local authorities. With the base rate rising to 5.0% (Appendix 3), internal funds avoid the cost of dearer debt.

Point 2: Retained profit keeps control with the cooperative's members and founder Nia Okafor, with no lender conditions on the $540,000 investment and no asset at risk if the electric trucks fail to reduce the 4.1% vehicle defect rate. It is available immediately, so the computerised stock control system can be installed before the next collection cycle, helping deliver the contamination-free service that 63% of surveyed officers will pay $0.30 more for.

The $340,000 loan is also exposed to a base rate that has risen from 4.25% to 5.0%, so using more internal funds reduces the cooperative's exposure to debt-service costs during the electric-fleet programme.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid point identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation and analysis applied to TGL and the case data.

questions.question_text: TGL is promoting a guaranteed contamination-free collection service to local authorities. Consider national television advertising, local radio sponsorship, or social media influencer marketing. Which should TGL choose to promote the service? Justify your recommendation.
questions.model_answer:
National television advertising: TV could raise awareness of recycling services quickly, but airtime is very expensive for a cooperative funding a $540,000 fleet and most viewers are not the local authority officers who award collection contracts. With demand for recycled materials up only 3.9%, much of the spend would be wasted nationally.

Local radio sponsorship: Local radio reaches residents and council officers within TGL's own service area, supports the 26,000 collections made each quarter and costs far less than television. It suits a message about cleaner local collection. Its limits are modest reach and a largely consumer audience, so it may not by itself persuade procurement officers awarding authority-wide contracts, particularly when 59% rank reliability above price.

Social media influencer marketing: Sustainability influencers can showcase contamination-free collections and recycling results to an engaged audience at low cost, reinforcing TGL's green brand. However, the audience is broad and not concentrated among the local authority officers who make purchasing decisions, so conversion to contracts may be slow.

Recommendation: TGL should choose local radio sponsorship. It targets the communities and officers in TGL's own contract area at a fraction of television's cost and fits a local authority service, while the $0.30 premium and 63% survey support give a clear message. Television is rejected as unaffordable and geographically wasteful, and influencers are rejected as too diffuse for local authority procurement; TGL can add targeted social content later.

Local radio also lets TGL respond quickly to the 23 monthly complaints still received and promote the falling 5.6% contamination rate as evidence of service improvement to the local authority officers who award contracts.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Identifies promotional options with limited reference to TGL's local authorities.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Discusses advantages and disadvantages of at least two options with TGL context and some judgement.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Evaluates all three options in the context of TGL's survey data and service area, with a justified recommendation explaining why television and influencers are rejected.

questions.question_text: TGL's 5.6% contamination rate and rising vehicle defects are damaging service. Explain two benefits for TGL of its flat structure and democratic leadership in addressing these problems.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Democratic leadership gives the 70 drivers and depot staff a voice in how loads are sorted and vehicles maintained, so they can propose practical ways to cut the 5.6% contamination rate, which is already down from 7.2%. Involvement raises motivation and ownership, helping staff take care with the 26,000 quarterly collections and protect the $0.30 premium that 63% of officers will pay.

Point 2: A flat structure shortens the chain of command so a 4.1% vehicle defect or an 8% fuel-waste issue can be reported and fixed quickly without several management layers. Combined with democratic leadership, this encourages drivers to share ideas on route planning and careful loading, cutting complaints from 41 to 23 a month and supporting the reliability that 59% of local authority officers rank above price.

Consulting drivers about collection routes also makes it easier to introduce the $0.30 contamination-free premium, because staff who understand the reason for cleaner loads are more likely to enforce it and protect the 63% of officers who value it.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid point identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation and analysis applied to TGL and the case data.

questions.question_text: TGL wants to reduce contamination and vehicle defects. Consider job rotation or team working. Which should TGL choose? Justify your decision.
questions.model_answer:
Job rotation: Moving drivers between collection routes and depot sorting would build multi-skilled staff who understand both driving and load quality, which could cut the 5.6% contamination rate and the 4.1% vehicle defect rate. It also reduces repetitiveness and helps cover for absence across the 70 staff. The drawbacks are slower initial work while staff learn new tasks and the need for more on-the-job training on the electric trucks, which could disrupt the 26,000 quarterly collections.

Team working: Organising drivers into teams with shared responsibility for load quality encourages peers to check contamination before collection and to report defects early. It fits TGL's cooperative values and democratic leadership, can lift morale and directly reduce the 41 monthly complaints. Its limits are that teams may develop group norms that tolerate errors, and it does not by itself build the deep technical skill needed to maintain the new electric trucks.

Decision: TGL should choose team working. Shared responsibility attacks the 5.6% contamination rate and 4.1% defect rate through peer checks and suits a cooperative, protecting the $0.30 premium; job rotation is rejected because the retraining disruption and shallower vehicle expertise would risk the current 26,000 collections while defects are already rising. TGL can add limited rotation later once teams are established.

To avoid the disruption of retraining, TGL can start with two volunteer teams and compare their contamination rates against the 26,000 quarterly collections before rolling the approach out. If the 4.1% defect rate falls, the practice can spread; if not, the cooperative can revert without having committed the whole workforce of 70.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Describes the two HR options with little application to TGL.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Analyses benefits and drawbacks of both options in TGL's context with some judgement.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Comprehensively evaluates both options against quality, cost and skills, with a clear decision and explicit reasons for rejecting the alternative.

questions.question_text: Calculate and explain how TGL's management can use its cost, break-even and productivity data.

sub_parts.model_answer: Formula: Margin of safety = Actual output − Break-even output. Break-even = Fixed costs ÷ Contribution per unit = $200,000 ÷ ($9.00 − $4.00) = $200,000 ÷ $5.00 = 40,000 units. Substitution: 100,000 − 40,000 = 60,000 units. Answer: margin of safety is 60,000 collections a year.
Formula: Contribution per unit = Selling price − Variable cost per unit. Substitution: $9.00 − $4.00 = $5.00. Answer: contribution per unit is $5.00.

sub_parts.question_text: Explain four ways TGL's management can use this financial data.
sub_parts.model_answer:
1. A margin of safety of 60,000 collections against 100,000 actual shows TGL can lose a large share of local authority work before a loss.
2. Contribution of $5.00 a collection lets managers model the $0.30 premium for contamination-free collections and judge discounts to councils.
3. Knowing break-even of 40,000 helps test whether the $340,000 bank loan can be serviced before more electric trucks are bought for the $540,000 fleet.
4. Average total cost of $6.00 a unit ($200,000 ÷ 100,000 = $2.00 plus $4.00) can be tracked against the 10.1% input-cost rise and the 8% fuel waste.

questions.model_answer: (i) Margin of safety = 60,000 collections | (ii) Contribution per unit = $5.00 | (iii) Four contextual uses: cushion of 60,000 collections; modelling the $0.30 contamination-free premium; servicing the $340,000 loan; and unit-cost control at $6.00 against 10.1% inflation and 8% fuel waste.

working_marks: 1 mark for correct formula and 1 mark for the accurate numerical answer in (i) and (ii); 1 mark for each valid applied use in (iii).

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 2, evaluate TGL's financial performance by calculating the gross profit margin, profit margin and ROCE for 2024 and 2025. Has TGL's financial performance improved? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Calculations:
Gross Profit Margin 2024 = 25.0%
Gross Profit Margin 2025 = 30.0%
Profit Margin 2024 = 10.0%
Profit Margin 2025 = 14.0%
ROCE 2024 = 12.0%
ROCE 2025 = 16.0%

Detailed workings: 2024 gross profit $600,000 ÷ revenue $2,400,000 × 100 = 25.0; 2025 $840,000 ÷ $2,800,000 × 100 = 30.0. Operating profit $240,000 ÷ revenue $2,400,000 × 100 = 10.0 in 2024 and $392,000 ÷ $2,800,000 × 100 = 14.0 in 2025. Returns on capital: $240,000 ÷ $2,000,000 × 100 = 12.0 in 2024 and $392,000 ÷ $2,450,000 × 100 = 16.0 in 2025. Cost of sales rose from $1,800,000 to $1,960,000 while revenue grew $400,000, so gross profit increased by $240,000. Interest payable fell from $22,000 to $18,000.

Evaluation: All three measures improved. The gross margin rose from 25.0% to 30.0%, showing better control of collection and processing costs despite 10.1% diesel and recycling inflation. The operating margin improved from 10.0% to 14.0%, so more revenue survives the $200,000 fixed costs. Returns on capital increased from 12.0% to 16.0%, meaning the $2,450,000 capital employed is generating more profit. These gains reflect real growth in revenue and gross profit. The concern is that contamination is still 5.6% and the vehicle defect rate 4.1%, which could raise costs and reverse the trend if the $540,000 fleet is badly managed.

Conclusion: TGL's financial performance has improved. The gross margin (25.0% to 30.0%), operating margin (10.0% to 14.0%) and returns on capital (12.0% to 16.0%) all rose together on the back of higher revenue and gross profit. TGL should protect the gain by using retained profit to cut the 5.6% contamination and 8% fuel waste.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: States financial figures or simple changes without accurate ratio calculations.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Calculates all three ratios for both years with some contextual analysis of the trend.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Accurate ratio calculations for both years plus detailed evaluation of revenue, costs, capital and interest, and a justified conclusion on whether performance improved.

questions.question_text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage for TGL of switching to electric collection trucks.
questions.model_answer:
Advantage: Electric trucks cut exposure to the 10.1% rise in diesel and recycling input costs and reduce the 8% fuel waste, protecting the $4.00 variable cost and the $5.00 contribution on each of the 100,000 collections. A cleaner fleet strengthens TGL's green brand with local authorities, supports the $0.30 premium for contamination-free service and helps justify the $540,000 investment funded partly by a $340,000 bank loan.

Disadvantage: The trucks are part of the $540,000 outlay alongside the loan while the base rate rises to 5.0%, so cash flow could be tight if demand for recycled materials grows only 3.9%. Charging and maintenance need drivers trained on the new trucks, yet 19 of 70 lack training and the 4.1% vehicle defect rate is rising; until the 5.6% contamination rate is tackled, the new trucks could add disruption rather than immediate savings.

Lower fuel use would also protect the $5.00 contribution per collection against the 10.1% input-cost rise and the 8% fuel waste, helping TGL hold the $9.00 price for local authorities as demand for recycled materials grows 3.9%.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid point identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation and analysis applied to TGL and the case data.

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 3, evaluate how the rise in the base interest rate to 5.0%, the 5.9% minimum wage increase and the 10.1% rise in diesel and recycling input costs will affect TGL. Which change will have the greatest impact? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Base interest rate (4.25% to 5.0%): If TGL's $340,000 bank loan is variable-rate, the annual interest cost rises by 0.75% of $340,000 = $2,550 a year (0.0075 × $340,000). That is modest beside fixed costs of $200,000 a year and zero on a fixed-rate loan. Higher rates could make local authorities delay contracts and raise future borrowing costs, but the direct interest effect is bounded.

Minimum wage increase (5.9%, to $13.35 an hour): With a workforce of 70 in driving and processing, this raises the wage bill and cannot be avoided. The insert gives no hours worked or individual pay, so no annual total can be invented; the fair comparison is productivity, 100,000 collections ÷ 70 staff = about 1,429 collections per worker. If that holds, the rise is manageable; if rising defects and contamination reduce efficiency, unit labour cost rises and the $5.00 contribution falls.

Input-cost inflation (10.1% diesel and recycling inputs): The $4.00 variable cost is not decomposed in the insert, so only a bound is honest: if the whole $4.00 rose 10.1%, that adds 10.1% × $4.00 = $0.404 a collection; across 100,000 collections a year that is about $40,400 (100,000 × $0.404). That would cut contribution from $5.00 to about $4.60 on every collection and compounds on the existing 8% fuel waste. Part can be recovered through the $0.30 contamination-free premium.

Conclusion: The 10.1% rise in diesel and recycling input costs will have the greatest impact. It applies to all 100,000 collections and erodes the $5.00 contribution that supports the $540,000 fleet, whereas the interest rise is a bounded $2,550 a year and the wage rise can be absorbed if productivity stays around 1,429 collections per worker. TGL should cut the 8% fuel waste first.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Identifies the three external changes with limited application to TGL.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Analyses the impact of at least two changes on TGL's costs, revenue or financing in context, using insert figures.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Evaluates all three changes in TGL's context with a well-justified judgement that input cost inflation has the greatest impact and clear reasons why the other two are smaller.
